premise.title: The Wrong-Way Ball
premise.logline: Tunde must score one goal past Amaka before sunset in the street final, but his new ball keeps bouncing away from the goal—until he aims at the puddle.
premise.theme: You cannot boss a bouncing ball; you can only play with where it wants to go.
premise.hook: Tunde winds up for a rocket shot—and the ball ricochets off the crate, the car, and into Mama Ngozi's tomatoes before he even finishes his follow-through.

spine: Once upon a time, in a sunny Lagos street, a boy named Tunde got a brand-new football from Mama Ngozi's stall.
Every day, Tunde and his friend Chidi played street football against Amaka, and every day Amaka won.
Until one day, the street's After-School Cup final arrived, and Tunde promised to score one goal past Amaka before sunset.
Because of that, Tunde shot at the goal—and his new ball bounced off the crate, the car, and into Mama Ngozi's tomatoes.
Because of that, Tunde tried again and again, but the ball always bounced the wrong way, while Amaka laughed and Chidi kept shouting 'I'm open!' from behind the goalpost.
Until finally, Chidi noticed the ball only went toward the goal when Tunde aimed at the puddle, so Tunde aimed at the puddle—and the ball bounced off the wall, past Amaka, and into the goal.
Ever since then, Tunde plays by reading the bounce, and the ball only ends up in the tomatoes when Amaka kicks it.
